title: Debugging misaligned completions with sparse-autoencoder latent attribution
one_liner: 比较同一模型正常与异常回答的 SAE 特征归因，再用 steering 检验哪些内部特征实际影响异常行为。

problem.text: 模型产生异常行为时，哪些内部 SAE 特征真正影响了这个回答？本文研究狭窄微调后泛化的失调行为，以及对模拟用户观点的不当肯定。来源是 OpenAI 2025 年 12 月 1 日的完整技术报告，非单独声称已同行评审的会议论文。

gap.text: 按微调前后激活差异筛选特征，可能挑中变化大但与异常无关的特征，也要求有一个相近的正常模型作比较。本文在一个模型内部比较同一提示的异常与正常续写，以更贴近具体行为的方式提出候选，再单独做因果干预。

method.text: 对每个续写计算其负对数似然相对中层激活的梯度，用一阶展开近似把某特征投影替换为均值后损失如何变化。将异常/正常续写的归因做差并跨样本平均，选 top-100 特征。之后分别压低或增强这些方向，生成新回答并由 GPT-5 评分，检验行为是否随之改变。

trace.text: 同一健康信息误导微调模型，对同一提示采样出正常和失调续写，共得到 35 对。按归因差选特征后，逐个负向 steering 看失调能否减少；也在另一正常模型正向 steering 看能否诱发失调。这样避免仅凭“这个特征的名字很像风险”下结论。

inputs_outputs.text: 输入为同模型成对续写、可访问的中层激活/梯度和 SAE 解码方向；输出为候选特征排名、steering 生成文本和行为评分。第二案例使用 148 对不当肯定/恰当回答，重复比较归因差与激活差两种筛选方式。

results.text: 两个案例中，归因差选出的 top-100 比激活差选出的集合含有更多能朝预期方向改变行为的特征，平均 steering 效果也更大。同一个排名最高的“provocative”特征出现在两种行为中。正文将其效果表述为失调增加 53%、不当肯定增加 40%；此卡不将图中的该表述擅自换算成百分点。

contributions.text: 提供无需成对模型的行为定位流程，把低成本一阶归因用作昂贵干预实验的候选筛选器。两种异常行为共享高影响特征的发现，说明看似不同的外部失败可能具有共同内部关联。

limitations.text: 归因是局部一阶近似，只有梯度在相关区间近似恒定时才较准确；饱和非线性可能使它失真，因此必须再验证 steering。案例少、评分依赖模型判分；同一方向可改变行为也不等于已完整解释其机制，更没有给出所有失调都适用的修复器。

cost.text: 作者通常使用 2M 特征的 SAE；对每个特征做完整前向消融代价太大，所以先用梯度近似筛选，再做候选生成与评分。需要权重/激活/梯度访问，报告不足以让外部读者完整复现其全部内部目标模型。

relevance.text: 知识库分析：桥接工具，提供“发现异常→定位内部特征→干预→重新评估”的直接实证。它涉及人或外部程序调试模型，未验证模型利用解释自主改进自身，也没有多轮 RSI 的累计收益证据。

related.reason: 以前者的特征分解与 steering 为基础，进一步用成对回答的归因差筛选与特定行为有关的方向。
CoT 可能漏报真实影响因素；本文从内部梯度与干预获得另一类证据，但也需要独立行为检验。

classification_reason: 对比异常与正常回答的特征归因，并通过干预检验行为影响，属于诊断与行为调试桥接证据。

en.one_liner: The report compares SAE feature attributions for normal and abnormal continuations from one model, then uses steering to test which features affect the behavior.

sections.problem: Which internal SAE features influence an abnormal answer? The report studies generalized misalignment after narrow fine-tuning and inappropriate affirmation of a simulated user’s views. The source is OpenAI’s full technical report dated December 1, 2025.
sections.gap: Selecting features by activation differences between fine-tuned and normal models can favor large but behaviorally irrelevant changes and requires a nearby normal model. This method instead compares normal and abnormal continuations for the same prompt within one model, then tests candidates through intervention.
sections.method: For each continuation, the authors differentiate its negative log-likelihood with respect to middle-layer activations. A first-order approximation estimates the loss change from replacing a feature projection with its mean. Attribution differences between abnormal and normal continuations are averaged across samples to select 100 features. Suppressing or amplifying these directions produces new answers that GPT-5 scores for behavioral change.
sections.trace: A model fine-tuned on misleading health information yields 35 pairs of normal and misaligned continuations. Features selected by attribution difference are individually suppressed to test whether misalignment decreases. Positive steering in another normal model tests whether the directions can induce it.
sections.inputs_outputs: Inputs are paired continuations from one model, accessible middle-layer activations and gradients, and SAE decoder directions. Outputs include feature rankings, steered generations and behavior scores. A second case uses 148 pairs of inappropriate and appropriate affirmations to compare attribution-difference and activation-difference selection.
sections.results: In both cases, attribution-selected top-100 sets contain more features that change behavior in the expected direction, with stronger average steering effects. A top-ranked provocative feature appears in both behaviors. The report describes increases of 53% in misalignment and 40% in inappropriate affirmation. These figures are retained as reported percentages, without conversion to percentage points.
sections.contributions: The workflow localizes behavior without requiring matched model pairs. Low-cost first-order attribution screens candidates for expensive interventions. A shared high-impact feature across two behaviors suggests an internal association between outwardly different failures.
sections.limitations: Attribution is a local first-order approximation and works best when gradients are roughly constant over the relevant range. Saturating nonlinearities can break it, requiring steering checks. The cases are few and scoring relies on a model judge. Changing behavior through a direction does not fully explain its mechanism or establish a general repair method.
sections.cost: The authors typically use a 2M-feature SAE. Full forward ablation of every feature is too expensive, motivating gradient screening before candidate generation and judging. Weight, activation and gradient access are required. External readers cannot fully reproduce all internal target-model experiments from the report.
sections.relevance: Library analysis. This is a bridge from detecting abnormal behavior to locating internal features, intervening and reevaluating. The work involves human or external-program debugging and does not establish autonomous explanation-driven self-improvement or cumulative gains over multiple RSI rounds.

related.scaling-monosemanticity: The study builds on feature decomposition and steering, using attribution differences between paired answers to select behavior-relevant directions.
related.cot-faithfulness: CoT may omit influential factors. Internal gradients and interventions offer a different source of evidence, which also needs independent behavioral validation.
